In any event, the full application of the minimum sanctions/remedies regimes provided by those provisions shall remain unaffected and may not be reduced as a result of the set-offs referred to in this paragraph.

12. The procedural guarantees provided by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970 shall remain in force and may under no circumstances be derogated from in peius by the provisions of this article. The provisions of this article shall apply as special sectoral rules exclusively with regard to the disciplinary procedure for imposing dismissal for just cause and for subjective justified reason, in an integrative and more protective sense relative to the general discipline. With regard to individual dismissal and the related remedies, the provisions of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966, Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, Law No. 92 of 28 June 2012, and Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015 shall also remain applicable to auto-tramway personnel according to their respective temporal and personal scopes of application, as well as the relevant provisions of the national sectoral collective agreements, insofar as not derogated from by this article.


Art. Y  
(Repeals and discipline applicable to auto-tramway personnel)

1. As from the date of entry into force of this law, Royal Decree No. 148 of 8 January 1931, as subsequently amended, is repealed in its entirety. Also repealed, insofar as they specially govern the employment relationship, the disciplinary procedure, or protection against dismissal of auto-tramway personnel, are those statutory and regulatory provisions incompatible with this law.

2. With regard to individual dismissal, auto-tramway personnel shall be subject to the provisions of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966, Article 18 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, as amended by Law No. 92 of 28 June 2012, and Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015, according to their respective temporal and personal scopes of application, as well as any further provisions of law in force concerning protection against unlawful dismissals, with no sector-specific derogations other than the procedural ones provided for in Article X. The statutory provisions that exclude or limit the application to auto-tramway personnel of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966, Article 18 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, and Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015 are consequently repealed.

3. The provisions of Article X constitute special sectoral rules exclusively with regard to the disciplinary procedure for imposing dismissal for just cause and for subjective justified reason, in an integrative and non-worsening sense relative to the guarantees provided by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970. For every other aspect of the employment relationship of auto-tramway personnel, the rules of ordinary law and the sectoral collective bargaining agreements shall apply.

1. Overall assessment with respect to the stated principles  

– Requirement no. 1 (complete repeal of Royal Decree No. 148/1931) is formally satisfied by Article Y, paragraph 1, which repeals it “in its entirety.”  
– Requirement no. 2 (consistency with Article 2119 of the Civil Code, Law No. 604/1966, Law No. 300/1970, and Legislative Decree No. 23/2015) is broadly respected:  
  • Article X correctly refers to Article 2119 of the Civil Code for just cause;  
  • it refers to the definition of subjective justified reason in Law No. 604/1966;  
  • it coordinates, at least in principle, with Articles 7 and 18 of Law No. 300/1970;  
  • it acknowledges the applicability of Legislative Decree No. 23/2015, “according to the respective temporal and personal scopes of application,” thereby avoiding overlaps.  

The structure is already good; the useful amendments mainly concern:  
– greater precision in coordinating with the general rules (especially Articles 7 and 18 of the Workers’ Statute and Legislative Decree No. 23/2015);  
– better legislative technique with regard to repeal and transitional discipline;  
– some corrections to ensure that the procedural guarantees introduced are genuinely “more protective” and not ambiguous.

Below are constructive observations, with specific proposals for redrafting.

---

2. Article X – Consistency and points to strengthen  

### 2.1. Consistency with Article 2119 of the Civil Code  

– Paragraph 1 substantially reproduces the content of Article 2119, while making “full” reference to it.  
– This is systematically correct, but somewhat redundant. To avoid interpretative uncertainty, it would be better to confine yourself to a straightforward reference, without paraphrase, or to clarify that the definition is purely reproducing the code provision without introducing variants.

**Suggested adjustment to paragraph 1**  
Replace the descriptive part with a more concise formula, for example:  

> “1. For auto-tramway personnel, dismissal for just cause shall be governed by Article 2119 of the Civil Code. The employer may impose it, by means of a written act and without notice, where the conditions laid down therein are met.”

This removes any risk of a sector-specific interpretation diverging from the Civil Code notion.

---

### 2.2. Consistency with Law No. 604/1966  

– Paragraph 2 correctly states that:  
  • the notion of subjective justified reason remains that provided by Law No. 604/1966;  
  • the remedies following unlawful dismissal follow the general regimes (Law No. 604, Article 18 of the Workers’ Statute, Legislative Decree No. 23/2015) “according to their respective temporal and personal scopes of application.”  

– This avoids the risk of unduly extending Law No. 604, solely for the auto-tramway category, to subjects normally excluded; the reference “according to the respective scopes…” is technically correct.

**Suggested improvement**  
To dispel doubts, one could explicitly state that the special discipline is procedural only:

> “2. (…) In any event, the provisions of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966 and of the other rules in force shall remain applicable, with regard to the substantive conditions for termination and the regime of protection against unlawful dismissal, according to their respective temporal and personal scopes of application.”

This makes clear that no separate category is being created on the substantive level.

---

### 2.3. Consistency with Law No. 300/1970 (Articles 7 and 18)  

**Disciplinary procedure (Article 7)**  

– Paragraphs 3–9 add more detailed procedural rules than Article 7 of the Workers’ Statute (time limits, methods of service, opinion of the Disciplinary Committee).  
– Article X, paragraph 12, and Article Y, paragraph 3, expressly state:  
  • the integrative and non-worsening nature of the discipline with respect to Article 7;  
  • the prohibition of derogations in peius.  

At the level of principles, consistency is respected. Two points still need strengthening:

1. **Relationship between statute and collective bargaining**  
   – The draft provides that collective agreements and company regulations are to define the composition and rules of the Committee.  
   – It would be useful to state expressly that collective clauses worsening the minimum guarantees of Article X and Article 7 are null and void.

   **Proposed addition to paragraph 12**:  

   > “Any provisions of collective agreements or company regulations that directly or indirectly reduce the minimum procedural guarantees laid down by this article or by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970 shall be null and void.”

2. **Procedural time limits for the statement of charges and the dismissal measure**  
   – Thirty-day period (extendable to sixty with reasons) for the statement of charges (paragraph 4): this is an improvement over the silence of Article 7 and creates no conflict.  
   – Mandatory thirty-day period for dismissal after the explanations/hearing/Committee opinion (paragraph 8): again, this is a greater protection than Article 7.  
   – It should, however, be clarified that any shorter periods provided by collective agreements are permitted insofar as they are more favorable to the employee (they reinforce the principle of promptness).

   **Possible small clarification in paragraph 4 or 8**:  

   > “Collective agreements may provide for shorter periods, insofar as more favorable to the employee, in compliance with the principles of promptness and proportionality of disciplinary action.”

**Post-dismissal protections (Article 18)**  

– Article X does not alter the content of the remedies; it correctly refers back to the provisions in force (Article 18, as amended by Law No. 92/2012).  
– Paragraph 11, concerning the set-off between remuneration due for the precautionary suspension period and allowances/compensation under Article 18 or Legislative Decree No. 23, is conceptually correct:  
  • it avoids unjustified cumulation;  
  • it protects the statutory “minimum” amount of the allowances.

To strengthen consistency with Article 18 (which distinguishes between various hypotheses of reinstatement and compensation), it would be useful to specify that such set-offs operate only “up to the amount due” and without affecting the statutory minima:

> “The sums due (…) shall be allocated and set off, up to the overall amount, against the allowances and compensation awarded to the employee (…) without prejudice, in any event, to the employee’s right to receive in full the minimum amounts provided by those provisions.”

---

### 2.4. Consistency with Legislative Decree No. 23/2015  

– References to Legislative Decree No. 23/2015 are frequent (paragraphs 2, 11, 12; Article Y, paragraph 2) and are always accompanied by the clause “according to the respective temporal and personal scopes of application.”  
– The sectoral discipline does not affect:  
  • the criteria for quantifying the allowance under the growing-protections regime;  
  • the conditions for its application (date of hiring, size of employer, etc.).  

The only delicate profile is again the set-off in paragraph 11: for workers under the growing-protections regime, the allowance is “all-inclusive.” It is therefore important to avoid readings that would seem to reduce it below the statutory minima.

The clarification proposed above (“without prejudice to the right to the statutory minima”) safeguards this consistency.

---

### 2.5. Specific technical observations on Article X  

1. **Disciplinary Committee (paragraphs 6–7)**  
   – It is an appreciable strengthening of guarantees, but:  
     • its effectiveness depends on its timely establishment by the collective agreements or company regulations;  
     • failing that, the worker’s right risks remaining purely theoretical.  

   **Suggestion**: provide for a maximum time limit for establishing the Committees and a default discipline:  

   > “Within six months from the entry into force of this law, the national sectoral collective agreements or, failing that, company regulations adopted following agreement with the company trade union representatives, shall lay down the discipline governing the Disciplinary Committee. If that period expires without action, the Committee shall in any event be established according to criteria laid down by decree of the Minister of Labour, after hearing the comparatively most representative trade union organizations.”

2. **Precautionary suspension (paragraph 10)**  
   – Balanced regulation:  
     • general rule = suspension with pay;  
     • suspension without pay or with reduced treatment allowed only if provided for by collective agreements, with limits and compliance with Article 36 of the Constitution;  
     • beyond thirty days, suspension is in any event paid, save for obstructive conduct by the employee.  

   Two points can still be improved:  
   – The case in which, once the procedure ends, **no dismissal follows** or only a lesser sanction is imposed (warning, fine, disciplinary suspension) is not regulated. It would be appropriate to clarify that any unpaid precautionary suspension must in any event be retrospectively paid, at least if the facts do not amount to just cause or subjective justified reason.  
   – Proof of the employee’s “obstructive conduct” should be made more rigorous, to avoid abuse.

   **Proposed addition to paragraph 10**:  

   > “Where, at the end of the disciplinary procedure, no dismissal for just cause or subjective justified reason is imposed, or where a conservative sanction is applied, the period of precautionary suspension shall in any event be treated as active service and shall be paid in full.  
   > Where the employer alleges obstructive conduct attributable to the employee for the purpose of deferring the final measure beyond the thirtieth day, such conduct must be specifically indicated and proved.”

3. **Relationship with Article 7 of Law No. 300 (paragraph 12)**  
   – The wording “special sectoral discipline exclusively with regard to the disciplinary procedure” is correct.  
   – To avoid interpretative litigation, one might close with a prevalence clause:  

   > “In the event of interpretative conflict between the provisions of this article and Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, the provision ensuring the higher level of protection for the employee shall prevail.”

---

3. Article Y – Repeals and systematic coordination  

### 3.1. Complete repeal of Royal Decree No. 148/1931 (principle 1)  

– Article Y, paragraph 1, repeals Royal Decree No. 148/1931 “in its entirety,” thereby satisfying the constraint imposed by principle no. 1.  
– However, from the standpoint of legislative technique and the overall stability of the legal system, it would be appropriate to:  
  • verify whether Royal Decree No. 148/1931 contains provisions that are not strictly labour-law provisions (for example, matters concerning service organization, safety, service schedules, etc.) and that have not already been fully transposed into other sources;  
  • if so, reproduce those contents, where still necessary, elsewhere (for example in highway or public transport legislation, or in implementing regulations), so as to avoid regulatory gaps while maintaining the complete repeal.

**Suggestion**  
Add a paragraph (even a principled one) entrusting the recognition and possible regulatory reordering of those provisions:

> “By means of one or more legislative decrees or regulations to be adopted within twelve months from the entry into force of this law, a review shall be carried out of the provisions of Royal Decree No. 148 of 8 January 1931 other than those governing the employment relationship, in order to ensure, where still necessary, their coordination or reordering within the existing legislation on public transport services.”

This respects the intention to repeal the Royal Decree in full, while offering the legislator an orderly path to avoid gaps on extra-labour-law matters.

---

### 3.2. Repeal of incompatible special rules / generic clauses  

– Article Y, paragraph 1, second sentence, and paragraph 2, second sentence, use generic formulas (“insofar as…”, “provisions that exclude or limit…”).  
– From the standpoint of legal certainty, it would be preferable to:  
  • expressly list the provisions repealed, at least the main ones, after a systematic review;  
  • limit the general clauses to residual cases only.

**Suggestion**  

– Replace (or supplement) the generic clause with an enumeration, for example:  

> “Also repealed are those statutory provisions that exclude or limit the application to auto-tramway personnel of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966, Article 18 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, and Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015, including in particular: [specific list after review].”

– Retain a closing clause such as:  

> “All further provisions incompatible with this law are likewise repealed.”

This makes the task easier for interpreters and reduces litigation.

---

### 3.3. Relationship with public employment and other sectoral legislation  

Although the stated principles do not expressly require coordination with Legislative Decree No. 165/2001 or with local public transport legislation, it is realistic that some auto-tramway personnel work in public bodies or publicly controlled companies.

To avoid doubts:

**Suggestion of at least a coordination clause**  

> “The provisions of this law shall apply to auto-tramway personnel employed by public and private employers, without prejudice to Legislative Decree No. 165 of 30 March 2001 as regards public employment, and to the rules in force concerning local public transport services.”

This clarifies that the new discipline does not conflict with the public employment framework, but supplements the auto-tramway sector only as regards dismissal.

---

### 3.4. Transitional discipline (currently missing)  

At present, the proposal does not regulate:  
– disciplinary procedures and dismissals already initiated before entry into force;  
– dismissal challenges already pending;  
– the effects of repealing Royal Decree No. 148/1931 on ongoing relationships.

To avoid litigation and intertemporal application problems:

**Proposal for a concise transitional article (or paragraphs)**  

> “1. Disciplinary procedures pending on the date of entry into force of this law shall continue to be governed by the provisions in force at the time they were initiated, unless the employee requests, within thirty days, the application of the new discipline where more favorable.  
> 2. Dismissals imposed before the entry into force of this law and the related judicial or extrajudicial challenges shall continue to be governed by the rules in force at the time of dismissal.  
> 3. The effects of administrative acts and contractual acts validly adopted while Royal Decree No. 148 of 8 January 1931 was in force shall remain unaffected.”

This allows an orderly transition from the old regime to the new one.

---

4. Summary of the main interventions recommended to the legislator  

1. **Refine the reference to Article 2119 of the Civil Code (Article X, paragraph 1)** to avoid duplication and possible interpretative divergence.  
2. **Make explicit the purely procedural character of the special discipline** for just cause and subjective justified reason (Article X, paragraphs 2 and 12; Article Y, paragraph 3).  
3. **Strengthen the relationship with Article 7 of the Workers’ Statute**, by providing:  
   – an express prohibition of derogations in peius, including via collective agreements/company regulations;  
   – the possibility of shorter periods in melius for the statement of charges and the measure.  
4. **Specify the discipline of precautionary suspension**:  
   – mandatory full pay where no dismissal follows or only a conservative sanction is applied;  
   – specific burden of proof for obstructive conduct by the employee.  
5. **Make the Disciplinary Committee effective**, by providing:  
   – a time limit for its establishment;  
   – a possible supplementary ministerial regime.  
6. **Carefully handle the repeal of Royal Decree No. 148/1931**:  
   – confirm its total repeal;  
   – provide for a review and reordering of any extra-labour-law provisions still necessary.  
7. **Replace generic repeal clauses** with, as far as possible, a list of the rules that exclude or limit the application of Law No. 604/1966, Law No. 300/1970, and Legislative Decree No. 23/2015 to auto-tramway personnel.  
8. **Introduce a transitional discipline** for disciplinary procedures and dismissals already pending on the date of entry into force of the law.  
9. **Insert a coordination clause** with public employment and local public transport legislation, limiting the intervention to dismissal only.

With these adjustments, the proposal would be more systematically solid, consistent with the stated principles, and capable of fully and definitively replacing Royal Decree No. 148/1931 without creating gaps or overlaps in the discipline governing dismissal of auto-tramway personnel.

Art. X  
(Dismissal for just cause and for subjective justified reason of auto-tramway personnel)

1. For auto-tramway personnel, dismissal for just cause shall be governed by Article 2119 of the Civil Code, to which full reference is hereby made. The employer may impose it, by means of a written act and without notice, where the conditions laid down therein are met.

2. The provisions of this article shall also apply to disciplinary dismissal for subjective justified reason of auto-tramway personnel. In any event, the provisions of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966 and of the other rules in force, including Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015, shall remain applicable, as regards the substantive conditions for termination and the regime of protection against unlawful dismissal, according to their respective temporal and personal scopes of application.

3. Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 7, paragraphs 1 and 2, of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, dismissal for just cause and dismissal for subjective justified reason shall be preceded by a written statement of charges, to be communicated to the employee with a specific indication of the facts, the circumstances of time and place, and any statutory, contractual, or regulatory provisions alleged to have been violated. The statement of charges shall be served by registered letter with return receipt, certified electronic mail, or hand delivery with acknowledgment of receipt by the employee.

4. The statement of charges shall be timely and in any event made within thirty days from the date on which the fact is first known, in sufficiently defined terms, by the person holding disciplinary authority or by a person delegated by him or her. Where, because of the particular complexity of the investigation, a longer period is necessary, the statement of charges must provide an express and analytical statement of reasons, indicating the investigative activities carried out or to be carried out, in any event not later than sixty days from knowledge of the fact, without prejudice to compliance with the principles of promptness and proportionality of disciplinary action. Collective agreements may provide for shorter periods, insofar as more favorable to the employee.

5. In the notice of charges, the employee shall be granted a period of not less than five days from receipt to submit his or her explanations. Explanations may be given in writing or by requesting an oral hearing. The employee has the right to be assisted, in the hearing or in preparing written explanations, by a representative of the trade union association to which he or she belongs or to which he or she has given a mandate, or by counsel of his or her choice.

6. At the employee’s request, to be made within the period referred to in paragraph 5, the hearing shall take place before an internal Disciplinary Committee, composed on an equal basis of representatives of the employer and of the employees, appointed according to criteria established by the national sectoral collective agreements or, failing that, by company regulations adopted following agreement with the company trade union representatives. Failure to establish the Committee, or the impossibility of convening it within the time limits referred to in paragraph 7, for reasons not attributable to the employer or to the employee, shall not preclude continuation and completion of the disciplinary procedure, without prejudice to compliance with the guarantees provided by this article and by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970. Failure to request a hearing before the Committee may not be taken into account to the employee’s detriment.

7. The Disciplinary Committee referred to in paragraph 6, where seised, shall proceed with the hearing of the employee as promptly as possible and shall issue a reasoned opinion within ten days from the date of the hearing. If that period expires without the opinion having been issued, the employer may in any event adopt the disciplinary measure, stating that fact in the measure itself. The Committee’s opinion shall not be binding; where it is disregarded, the employer shall be required to provide specific reasons in the act imposing dismissal.

8. Where the conditions are met, the employer shall adopt the dismissal measure by means of a written and reasoned act, to be communicated to the employee in the manner referred to in paragraph 3, within the mandatory period of thirty days:
   a) from the expiry of the period granted for the submission of explanations, where no oral hearing is requested;  
   b) from the date of the employee’s hearing, where it takes place without the intervention of the Disciplinary Committee;  
   c) from the date of receipt of the Disciplinary Committee’s opinion or from the expiry of the period referred to in paragraph 7, where no opinion has been issued.  

   If the period referred to in this paragraph expires without action, the employer shall forfeit the power to impose dismissal in relation to the facts covered by the statement of charges. Collective agreements may provide for shorter periods, insofar as more favorable to the employee.

9. The dismissal measure shall indicate the facts charged, the reasons why they are considered established and such as to constitute just cause or subjective justified reason for termination, as well as the effective date of the dismissal and any absence of notice.

10. In cases of particular seriousness of the facts charged, or where the employee’s remaining in service may prejudice operational safety, the safety of third parties, or the integrity of company property, the employer may order, simultaneously with the statement of charges, the precautionary suspension of the employee from service, as a rule with pay maintained. Precautionary suspension without pay, or with reduced economic treatment, shall be allowed only where expressly provided by the national sectoral collective agreements, which shall lay down its maximum duration and the minimum guaranteed treatment, in compliance with Article 36 of the Constitution. Where precautionary suspension lasts for more than thirty days without the final measure having been adopted, it shall in any event be paid from the thirty-first day onward, unless the delay is due to obstructive conduct attributable to the employee, to be indicated and justified in the measure extending the suspension. Where, at the end of the disciplinary procedure, no dismissal for just cause or subjective justified reason is imposed, or where a conservative sanction is applied, the period of precautionary suspension shall in any event be treated as active service and shall be paid in full. For the purposes of this paragraph, obstructive conduct attributable to the employee must be specifically indicated and proved by the employer.

11. If the dismissal is subsequently declared unlawful, the period of precautionary suspension shall be treated for all purposes as active service; the employee shall be entitled to the related remuneration, net of any amounts already received by way of allowance or economic treatment connected with the suspension. The sums due on that basis shall be allocated and set off, up to the overall amount, against the allowances and compensation awarded to the employee as a consequence of the unlawfulness of the dismissal pursuant to Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966, Article 18 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, as amended by Law No. 92 of 28 June 2012, and Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015, according to their respective scopes of application, without prejudice, in any event, to the employee’s right to receive in full the minimum amounts provided by those provisions.

12. The procedural guarantees provided by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970 shall remain in force and may under no circumstances be derogated from in peius by the provisions of this article. The provisions of this article shall apply as special sectoral rules exclusively with regard to the disciplinary procedure for imposing dismissal for just cause and for subjective justified reason, in an integrative and more protective sense relative to the general discipline. With regard to individual dismissal and the related remedies, the provisions of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966, Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, Law No. 92 of 28 June 2012, and Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015 shall also remain applicable to auto-tramway personnel according to their respective temporal and personal scopes of application, as well as the relevant provisions of the national sectoral collective agreements, insofar as not derogated from by this article. Any provisions of collective agreements or company regulations that directly or indirectly reduce the minimum procedural guarantees laid down by this article or by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970 shall be null and void. In the event of interpretative conflict between the provisions of this article and Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, the provision ensuring the higher level of protection for the employee shall prevail.

13. Within six months from the entry into force of this law, the national sectoral collective agreements or, failing that, company regulations adopted following agreement with the company trade union representatives shall lay down the composition and operation of the Disciplinary Committee referred to in paragraphs 6 and 7. If that period expires without action, the Committee shall in any event be established according to criteria laid down by decree of the Minister of Labour and Social Policies, after hearing the trade union organizations of workers and employers that are comparatively the most representative at national level.

1. Concise assessment with respect to the stated principles  

a) Repeal of Royal Decree No. 148/1931  
– Article Y, paragraph 1, expressly satisfies the requirement: the Royal Decree is “repealed in its entirety.”  
– Article Z, paragraph 3, however, creates a technical friction: it refers to a “review of the provisions of the Royal Decree (…) in order to ensure their coordination or reordering.” After a repeal “in its entirety,” there can be no reordering of rules still in force, but only the possible transposition of substantive contents into new sources.  

b) Consistency with Article 2119 of the Civil Code, Law No. 604/1966, Law No. 300/1970, and Legislative Decree No. 23/2015  
– Article 2119 of the Civil Code: the full reference (Article X, paragraph 1) is correct and does not appear to be derogated from at the substantive level.  
– Law No. 604/1966: repeatedly referred to as the framework governing the conditions of lawfulness and the remedies (Article X, paragraphs 2, 11, 12; Article Y, paragraph 3); no substantive sectoral derogations emerge.  
– Law No. 300/1970, Article 7: the proposed discipline is expressly special only on the procedural level, “in an integrative and non-worsening sense” (Article X, paragraph 12; Article Y, paragraph 5), with an express prohibition of derogations in peius.  
– Legislative Decree No. 23/2015: the proposal refers to it correctly “according to the respective temporal and personal scopes of application” and does not appear to introduce generalized reinstatement protections incompatible with the growing-protections regime.  

Overall, consistency with the stated principles is good. Some points, however, require technical clarification to avoid interpretative litigation and implicit conflicts with the general discipline.

2. Strengths of the proposal  

– It clearly overcomes the special regime of Royal Decree No. 148/1931 with regard to the employment relationship, realigning auto-tramway personnel with ordinary dismissal law.  
– It codifies a clear disciplinary procedure, with defined time limits, adversarial guarantees, and the possibility of strengthened union/legal assistance.  
– It expressly qualifies the new rules as “special sectoral” only on the procedural level, avoiding the creation of an autonomous substantive subsystem in conflict with Law No. 604/1966, Law No. 300/1970, and Legislative Decree No. 23/2015.  
– It introduces an articulated discipline of precautionary suspension, with attention to compliance with Article 36 of the Constitution and to the legal and economic treatment of the suspension period.

3. Critical issues and proposals for substantive amendment  

3.1. Repeal of Royal Decree No. 148/1931 and subsequent coordination  
**Critical issue**  
– Article Y, paragraph 1, provides for full repeal of Royal Decree No. 148/1931.  
– Article Z, paragraph 3, still refers to the “provisions of the Royal Decree” for their coordination/reordering, wording that may be read as implying the survival of some parts of the Royal Decree, in tension with the principle of “complete repeal.”  

**Proposed amendment (substantive and clarifying)**  
a) Keep Article Y, paragraph 1, as it stands (it is in line with principle 1).  
b) Reformulate Article Z, paragraph 3, so as to clarify that:  
– the Royal Decree is definitively repealed;  
– any technical-administrative contents still necessary do not remain in force but, if appropriate, are reproduced in new sources.  

Example of new wording for paragraph 3:  

> “3. By means of one or more legislative decrees or regulations to be adopted within twelve months from the date of entry into force of this law, the Government shall proceed to reorder and, where necessary, reproduce in new provisions those rules concerning public transport services which, prior to the repeal referred to in Article Y, paragraph 1, were contained in Royal Decree No. 148 of 8 January 1931 and are different from those governing the employment relationship. Such reordering shall in no event entail the revival, even partial, of the provisions of the said Royal Decree repealed by Article Y, paragraph 1. In any event, the effects of administrative acts and contractual acts validly adopted while the repealed Royal Decree was in force shall remain unaffected.”

This makes the total repeal of Royal Decree No. 148/1931 effective and not merely formal.

---

3.2. Personal scope and public employment (Article Y, paragraph 4)  
**Critical issue**  
– Paragraph 4 links application of the law to personnel employed by public and private employers, “without prejudice” to Legislative Decree No. 165/2001.  
– For privatized public employment, Legislative Decree No. 165/2001 already refers back to civil-law discipline (including Law No. 604/1966, Law No. 300/1970, Legislative Decree No. 23/2015); the rule therefore risks overlaps, especially as regards special disciplinary procedures already laid down in some public sectors.  

**Proposed amendment**  
– Clarify that:  
  * for privatized public employment, this discipline applies insofar as compatible with Title II of Legislative Decree No. 165/2001 (and with any special disciplinary procedures laid down therein);  
  * non-privatized employment relationships are excluded, where abstractly referable to transport services.

Example of addition to paragraph 4:

> “4. The provisions of this law shall apply to auto-tramway personnel employed by public and private employers. As regards personnel of public administrations referred to in Article 1, paragraph 2, of Legislative Decree No. 165 of 30 March 2001, this law shall apply within the limits and according to the criteria laid down in Articles 2 and 63 of that decree and insofar as compatible with the special disciplinary provisions laid down therein and by the relevant collective bargaining agreements.”

---

3.3. Time limits for the statement of charges and the principle of “promptness” (Article X, paragraph 4)  
**Critical issue**  
– Paragraph 4 introduces maximum periods (30/60 days) for the statement of charges, while at the same time describing it as “timely.”  
– Case law under Article 7 of Law No. 300/1970 has developed the requirement of promptness in concrete terms, even apart from rigid time limits; the current wording could be read as an “absolute presumption” of timeliness within 30/60 days, thereby weakening the standards developed by the Supreme Court.

**Proposed amendment**  
– Keep the time limits, but clarify that they operate as a maximum threshold and do not exclude a concrete judicial assessment of delay even within those limits.

Example of reformulation of paragraph 4:

> “4. The statement of charges shall be made without delay, in compliance with the principle of promptness of disciplinary action, and in any event within thirty days from the date on which the fact is first known, in sufficiently defined terms, by the person holding disciplinary authority or by a person delegated by him or her. Where, because of the particular complexity of the investigation, a longer period is necessary, the statement of charges must provide an express and analytical statement of reasons, indicating the investigative activities carried out or to be carried out, and must in any event be made not later than sixty days from knowledge of the fact. Judicial review, in concrete terms, of compliance with the principles of promptness and proportionality of disciplinary action shall in any case remain unaffected. Collective agreements may also provide for shorter periods, insofar as more favorable to the employee.”

---

3.4. Disciplinary Committee, duty to establish it, and sanction in case of omission (Article X, paragraphs 6, 7 and 13)  
**Critical issue**  
– An equal-membership Committee is provided for at the employee’s request, but:  
  * it is not entirely clear whether failure to establish it due to employer inertia (after the six months referred to in Article X, paragraph 13) affects the validity of the dismissal;  
  * there is a risk that the employer may attribute a failure to activate it to “causes not attributable” while in practice failing to act.

**Proposed amendments**  
1) Strengthen the duty of activation resting on the employer and responsibility for failure to establish the Committee.  
2) Specify the consequence in the event of breach, by analogy with Article 7 of Law No. 300/1970 (breach of essential procedural guarantees → unlawfulness of the dismissal).

Example of addition to paragraph 6:

> “… Failure to establish the Committee or the impossibility of convening it within the time limits referred to in paragraph 7 shall not preclude continuation and completion of the disciplinary procedure only where they are due to objective causes not attributable to the employer or to the employee, which must be specifically indicated in the notice referred to in paragraph 8. Otherwise, breach of the employee’s right to be heard before the Disciplinary Committee, where duly requested, shall entail the nullity of the dismissal for violation of the procedural guarantees laid down by this article and by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970.”

And, in paragraph 13, add:

> “If the period referred to in the first sentence expires without the employer having carried out the acts necessary for establishing the Committee, the omission shall be deemed attributable to the employer for the purposes of paragraph 6.”

---

3.5. Time limit for imposing dismissal and forfeiture (Article X, paragraph 8)  
**Critical issue**  
– Forfeiture of disciplinary power is provided for if dismissal is not imposed within thirty days from the events specified.  
– It is necessary to clarify:  
  * whether the forfeiture concerns only the facts already charged (and not subsequent or additional facts);  
  * whether a new statement of charges remains possible for distinct facts emerging later.

**Suggestion**  
– Clarify expressly that forfeiture concerns only the contested facts and does not preclude the exercise of disciplinary power in relation to different facts emerging subsequently, subject to compliance with the ordinary guarantees.

---

4. Operational conclusion  

The proposal is already strong and broadly consistent with the stated principles. To make it more solid and less exposed to future disputes, I would recommend above all:

1. Clarifying, in Article Z, paragraph 3, that the complete repeal of the Royal Decree does not allow any revival, but only the possible reproduction of non-labour-law contents in new sources.  
2. Better coordinating the subjective scope relating to public employment.  
3. Making clear that the 30/60-day periods for the statement of charges are maximum limits and do not eliminate concrete judicial scrutiny of promptness.  
4. Strengthening the rules on the actual establishment of the Disciplinary Committee and on the consequences of failure to establish it when duly requested by the worker.  
5. Specifying the scope of forfeiture under Article X, paragraph 8.

With these targeted interventions, the proposed text could become a coherent and robust legislative discipline capable of fully replacing Royal Decree No. 148/1931 while remaining fully aligned with the general framework of Italian labour law.

Art. X  
(Dismissal for just cause and for subjective justified reason of auto-tramway personnel)

1. For auto-tramway personnel, dismissal for just cause shall be governed by Article 2119 of the Civil Code, to which full reference is hereby made. The employer may impose it, by means of a written act and without notice, where the conditions laid down therein are met.

2. The provisions of this article shall also apply to disciplinary dismissal for subjective justified reason of auto-tramway personnel. In any event, the provisions of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966 and of the other rules in force, including Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015, shall remain applicable, as regards the substantive conditions for termination and the regime of protection against unlawful dismissal, according to their respective temporal and personal scopes of application.

3. Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 7, paragraphs 1 and 2, of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, dismissal for just cause and dismissal for subjective justified reason shall be preceded by a written statement of charges, to be communicated to the employee with a specific indication of the facts, the circumstances of time and place, and any statutory, contractual, or regulatory provisions alleged to have been violated. The statement of charges shall be served by registered letter with return receipt, certified electronic mail, or hand delivery with acknowledgment of receipt by the employee.

4. The statement of charges shall be made without delay, in compliance with the principle of promptness of disciplinary action, and in any event within thirty days from the date on which the fact is first known, in sufficiently defined terms, by the person holding disciplinary authority or by a person delegated by him or her. Where, because of the particular complexity of the investigation, a longer period is necessary, the statement of charges must provide an express and analytical statement of reasons, indicating the investigative activities carried out or to be carried out, and must in any event be made not later than sixty days from knowledge of the fact. Judicial review, in concrete terms, of compliance with the principles of promptness and proportionality of disciplinary action shall in any case remain unaffected. Collective agreements may provide for shorter periods, insofar as more favorable to the employee.

5. In the notice of charges, the employee shall be granted a period of not less than five days from receipt to submit his or her explanations. Explanations may be given in writing or by requesting an oral hearing. The employee has the right to be assisted, in the hearing or in preparing written explanations, by a representative of the trade union association to which he or she belongs or to which he or she has given a mandate, or by counsel of his or her choice.

6. At the employee’s request, to be made within the period referred to in paragraph 5, the hearing shall take place before an internal Disciplinary Committee, composed on an equal basis of representatives of the employer and of the employees, appointed according to criteria established by the national sectoral collective agreements or, failing that, by company regulations adopted following agreement with the company trade union representatives. Failure to establish the Committee or the impossibility of convening it within the time limits referred to in paragraph 7 shall not preclude continuation and completion of the disciplinary procedure only where they are due to objective causes not attributable to the employer or to the employee, which must be specifically indicated in the notice referred to in paragraph 8. Otherwise, breach of the employee’s right to be heard before the Disciplinary Committee, where duly requested, shall entail the nullity of the dismissal for violation of the procedural guarantees laid down by this article and by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970. Failure to request a hearing before the Committee may not be taken into account to the employee’s detriment.

7. The Disciplinary Committee referred to in paragraph 6, where seised, shall proceed with the hearing of the employee as promptly as possible and shall issue a reasoned opinion within ten days from the date of the hearing. If that period expires without the opinion having been issued, the employer may in any event adopt the disciplinary measure, stating that fact in the measure itself. The Committee’s opinion shall not be binding; where it is disregarded, the employer shall be required to provide specific reasons in the act imposing dismissal.

8. Where the conditions are met, the employer shall adopt the dismissal measure by means of a written and reasoned act, to be communicated to the employee in the manner referred to in paragraph 3, within the mandatory period of thirty days:
   a) from the expiry of the period granted for the submission of explanations, where no oral hearing is requested;  
   b) from the date of the employee’s hearing, where it takes place without the intervention of the Disciplinary Committee;  
   c) from the date of receipt of the Disciplinary Committee’s opinion or from the expiry of the period referred to in paragraph 7, where no opinion has been issued.  

   If the period referred to in this paragraph expires without action, the employer shall forfeit the power to impose dismissal in relation to the facts covered by the statement of charges, without prejudice to the exercise of disciplinary power in relation to other distinct facts that emerge subsequently. Collective agreements may provide for shorter periods, insofar as more favorable to the employee.

9. The dismissal measure shall indicate the facts charged, the reasons why they are considered established and such as to constitute just cause or subjective justified reason for termination, as well as the effective date of the dismissal and any absence of notice.

10. In cases of particular seriousness of the facts charged, or where the employee’s remaining in service may prejudice operational safety, the safety of third parties, or the integrity of company property, the employer may order, simultaneously with the statement of charges, the precautionary suspension of the employee from service, as a rule with pay maintained. Precautionary suspension without pay, or with reduced economic treatment, shall be allowed only where expressly provided by the national sectoral collective agreements, which shall lay down its maximum duration and the minimum guaranteed treatment, in compliance with Article 36 of the Constitution. Where precautionary suspension lasts for more than thirty days without the final measure having been adopted, it shall in any event be paid from the thirty-first day onward, unless the delay is due to obstructive conduct attributable to the employee, to be indicated and justified in the measure extending the suspension. Where, at the end of the disciplinary procedure, no dismissal for just cause or subjective justified reason is imposed, or where a conservative sanction is applied, the period of precautionary suspension shall in any event be treated as active service and shall be paid in full. For the purposes of this paragraph, obstructive conduct attributable to the employee must be specifically indicated and proved by the employer.

11. If the dismissal is subsequently declared unlawful, the period of precautionary suspension shall be treated for all purposes as active service; the employee shall be entitled to the related remuneration, net of any amounts already received by way of allowance or economic treatment connected with the suspension. The sums due on that basis shall be allocated and set off, up to the overall amount, against the allowances and compensation awarded to the employee as a consequence of the unlawfulness of the dismissal pursuant to Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966, Article 18 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, as amended by Law No. 92 of 28 June 2012, and Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015, according to their respective scopes of application, without prejudice, in any event, to the employee’s right to receive in full the minimum amounts provided by those provisions.

12. The procedural guarantees provided by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970 shall remain in force and may under no circumstances be derogated from in peius by the provisions of this article. The provisions of this article shall apply as special sectoral rules exclusively with regard to the disciplinary procedure for imposing dismissal for just cause and for subjective justified reason, in an integrative and more protective sense relative to the general discipline. With regard to individual dismissal and the related remedies, the provisions of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966, Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, Law No. 92 of 28 June 2012, and Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015 shall also remain applicable to auto-tramway personnel according to their respective temporal and personal scopes of application, as well as the relevant provisions of the national sectoral collective agreements, insofar as not derogated from by this article. Any provisions of collective agreements or company regulations that directly or indirectly reduce the minimum procedural guarantees laid down by this article or by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970 shall be null and void. In the event of interpretative conflict between the provisions of this article and Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, the provision ensuring the higher level of protection for the employee shall prevail.

13. Within six months from the entry into force of this law, the national sectoral collective agreements or, failing that, company regulations adopted following agreement with the company trade union representatives shall lay down the composition and operation of the Disciplinary Committee referred to in paragraphs 6 and 7. If that period expires without action and the employer has failed to carry out the acts necessary for establishing the Committee, the omission shall be deemed attributable to the employer for the purposes of paragraph 6. Failing regulation within that period, the Committee shall in any event be established according to criteria laid down by decree of the Minister of Labour and Social Policies, after hearing the trade union organizations of workers and employers that are comparatively the most representative at national level.


Art. Y  
(Repeals and discipline applicable to auto-tramway personnel)

1. As from the date of entry into force of this law, Royal Decree No. 148 of 8 January 1931, as subsequently amended, is repealed in its entirety.

2. Also repealed, insofar as they specially govern the employment relationship, the disciplinary procedure, or protection against dismissal of auto-tramway personnel, are those statutory and regulatory provisions incompatible with this law.

3. With regard to individual dismissal, auto-tramway personnel shall be subject to the provisions of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966, Article 18 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, as amended by Law No. 92 of 28 June 2012, and Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015, according to their respective temporal and personal scopes of application, as well as any further provisions of law in force concerning protection against unlawful dismissals, with no sector-specific derogations other than the procedural ones provided for in Article X. The statutory provisions that exclude or limit the application to auto-tramway personnel of Law No. 604 of 15 July 1966, Article 18 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970, and Legislative Decree No. 23 of 4 March 2015 are consequently repealed.

4. The provisions of this law shall apply to auto-tramway personnel employed by public and private employers. As regards personnel of public administrations referred to in Article 1, paragraph 2, of Legislative Decree No. 165 of 30 March 2001, this law shall apply within the limits and according to the criteria laid down in Articles 2 and 63 of that decree and insofar as compatible with the special disciplinary provisions laid down therein and by the relevant collective bargaining agreements.

5. The provisions of Article X constitute special sectoral rules exclusively with regard to the disciplinary procedure for imposing dismissal for just cause and for subjective justified reason, in an integrative and non-worsening sense relative to the guarantees provided by Article 7 of Law No. 300 of 20 May 1970. For every other aspect of the employment relationship of auto-tramway personnel, the rules of ordinary law and the sectoral collective bargaining agreements shall apply.


Art. Z  
(Transitional and coordination provisions)

1. Disciplinary procedures pending on the date of entry into force of this law shall continue to be governed by the provisions in force at the time they were initiated. Within thirty days from that date, the employee concerned may request, by means of a written act, that the discipline referred to in Article X be applied to those stages of the procedure not yet completed, where it is overall more favorable than the previous discipline, having regard to the adversarial guarantees, the procedural time limits, and the consequences of precautionary suspension. In any event, the acts already performed and the effects already produced under the previous discipline shall remain valid.

2. Dismissals imposed before the date of entry into force of this law and the related judicial or extrajudicial challenges shall continue to be governed by the rules in force at the time of dismissal.

3. By means of one or more legislative decrees or regulations to be adopted within twelve months from the date of entry into force of this law, the Government shall proceed to reorder and, where necessary, reproduce in new provisions those rules concerning public transport services which, prior to the repeal referred to in Article Y, paragraph 1, were contained in Royal Decree No. 148 of 8 January 1931 and are different from those governing the employment relationship. Such reordering shall in no event entail the revival, even partial, of the provisions of the said Royal Decree repealed by Article Y, paragraph 1. In any event, the effects of administrative acts and contractual acts validly adopted while the repealed Royal Decree was in force shall remain unaffected.
